An `<img>` sends the same file to every device: a phone downloads the picture made for a desktop screen, in the format you happened to save it in. `Image` from `next/image` resizes the picture for the screen, serves a modern format, loads it only when it comes near the viewport, and reserves its space so the layout does not jump.

An `<img>` that is a direct child of a `<picture>` is allowed.

## Examples

Reported:

{/* bad */}
```jsx
export default function Avatar({ user }) {
  return <img src="/avatars/default.png" alt={user.name} />;
}
```

Not reported:

{/* good */}
```jsx
import Image from "next/image";

export default function Avatar({ user }) {
  return <Image src="/avatars/default.png" alt={user.name} width={64} height={64} />;
}
```

{/* good */}
```jsx
export default function Hero() {
  return (
    <picture>
      <source srcSet="/hero.avif" type="image/avif" />
      <img src="/hero.jpg" alt="Our office" />
    </picture>
  );
}
```

## When not to use it

Image optimization runs on a server, and some hosts bill for it. If you export a static site or your images already come from an image CDN, a plain `<img>` can be the right choice.
